citations.claim: Total energy at first violating step 13 dropped to ~234.6 from E0 ~277.25, the reported energy_conserved violation.
Massive body 3 accelerated to speed ~11.1 by step 13 during head-on encounter.
Massive body 4 accelerated to speed ~10.2 by step 13 during head-on encounter.
Body 3 x-position advanced rapidly 11.68->11.96->12.26 over steps 11-13 while converging on body 4.
Body 4 x-position moved oppositely 12.74->12.49->12.21 over steps 11-13, head-on approach to 0.42 separation at step 13.

counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.030136 to 0.005 with all bodies, G, steps identical; finer integration resolves the close encounter so no violation.

explanation: Two heavy bodies (m~9.28 and ~8.25) start on head-on trajectories and undergo a close encounter reaching 0.42 separation at step 13, near the 0.3 softening length where forces/accelerations peak. With large outer dt~0.03 and only 6 substeps per step, the leapfrog substepping fails to resolve the steep force gradient and rapid velocity reversal (speeds ~8-11), causing a large discrete energy error (~42.6) exceeding the 2% tolerance. Reducing dt removes the failure, confirming temporal-resolution cause.
vision_note: Two central blue bodies move toward each other head-on across steps 10 to 12 and nearly overlap into a single clump at step 13. The remaining bodies stay far away and almost stationary while the dotted trails highlight the rapid convergence in the center.
